title: How Buy Now, Pay Later Makes Money (It's Not Interest)
description:
Pay-in-4 plans feel free, but lenders mostly earn from the store: a CFPB study found big BNPL lenders charged partner merchants about 3% per sale (2021). Some also charge late fees, and nearly half of users in a 2026 LendingTree survey said they paid late in the past year. The quiet risk is stacking several plans at once.

Sources: CFPB, 'Buy Now, Pay Later: Market Trends and Consumer Impacts' (Sept 2022); CFPB, 'Consumer Use of Buy Now, Pay Later and Other Unsecured Debt' (Jan 2025, 2022 data); LendingTree BNPL surveys (March 2026, self-reported, ~2,050 US adults each; page updated Nov 17, 2026). Not financial advice.

#buynowpaylater #bnpl #personalfinance #debt #moneytips

scenes.say: Split two hundred dollars into four payments of fifty, with no interest. So how does the lender make money?
Mostly from the store. A CFPB study found lenders charged partner stores about three percent per sale. About six dollars on two hundred.
Stores pay because it helps them sell. In a LendingTree survey, sixty-eight percent of users said BNPL makes them overspend.

visual.label: of users say BNPL makes them overspend

scenes.say: Some lenders also charge late fees. And forty-seven percent of users said they paid late in the past year, up from thirty-four percent in twenty twenty-four.
Then there's stacking. The CFPB found about six in ten borrowers had several loans open at once. Small payments add up fast.

visual.label: had several BNPL loans at once

scenes.say: The rule: only use it for things you could pay for today, and track every plan you have.
